angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 777,097 km at 62.90 pc = 0.17 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 15.8985 +/- 0.0170 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 62.90 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.117 +/- 0.009 solar radii from Garai et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-411 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...674A..44G/abstract): 777,097 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.098 +/- 0.04 solar masses from Garai et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-411 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...674A..44G/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6169 +/- 64 K from Garai et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-411 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...674A..44G/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Garai et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-411 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...674A..44G/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-411.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.383, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
